LanguageData.DynamicMending.AcceptFilterDesc: Choose what this machine will repair. Gear the recycled gear filter allows is recycled instead. Anything else that reaches its item spot - along with undamaged gear, gear above the auto-repair threshold and gear beyond its tech - is sent out the red reject chutes instead of blocking the spot.
LanguageData.DynamicMending.AcceptFilterHint: Gear this filter rejects leaves by the red chutes. Tainted apparel has its own setting on the machine.
LanguageData.DynamicMending.RecycleFilterDesc: Choose what this machine breaks down for materials instead of repairing, like a recycle bill on a mending station. Damaged or not, gear this filter allows is recycled, even if the accepted gear filter also allows it, and what it breaks down into leaves by the red reject chutes. Empty by default: nothing is recycled.
LanguageData.DynamicMending.RecycleFilterHint: Gear this filter allows is recycled, not repaired. Use the hit-point slider to recycle only worn-out gear. Tainted apparel has its own setting on the machine.
LanguageData.DynamicMending.OverclockDesc: Set how hard this machine runs, from 10% to 200%. Slower is more careful: at 10% it takes ten times as long but works like a skill 20 crafter, uses fewer materials and almost never botches a repair. Faster gets through gear quicker but works like a less skilled crafter. Power draw, heat and how often it breaks down all rise with the square of the speed, as power and heat do on Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Factory's machines, whose boosters and heatsinks also work on this one.
LanguageData.DynamicMending.OverclockInspect: Overclock {0}: works like a skill {1} crafter
LanguageData.DynamicMending.TaintedDesc: What to do with apparel taken from a corpse: repair it like anything else, break it down for materials, or send it straight out the reject chutes. Click to change.
